title: Evening Brief — Thu 26 Nov

stories.board: Bennett delays Eisenkot meeting until Sunday
stories.headline: Eisenkot's new Israeli government is not ready yet
stories.what: Three of the four parties against Netanyahu now have deals with Gadi Eisenkot. But Naftali Bennett pushed his meeting with Eisenkot to Sunday and still wants a unity government (all big parties together) with Netanyahu.
stories.why: Eisenkot needs 61 of 120 seats to lead, and without Bennett he is still short.
stories.sides: Eisenkot wants help from religious and Arab parties; Bennett prefers working with Netanyahu's Likud. No deal with the religious party UTJ yet.

stories.board: Canada study finds worrying campus views on Jews
stories.headline: Study of Canadian college students worries Jewish groups
stories.what: A government-paid study found two in three non-Jewish students think calling for Israel to stop existing is not antisemitic (hate against Jews). Minister Marc Miller said a report on anti-Jewish hate comes in December.
stories.why: Jewish groups say hate on campuses is growing and want action.
stories.sides: No major disagreement on the numbers. Some note the government scrapped its special envoy (helper) on antisemitism in June.

stories.board: SAP may cut 10,000 jobs for AI
stories.headline: Big software company SAP may cut at least 10,000 jobs
stories.what: Bloomberg reports German company SAP may cut about 9 out of every 100 jobs as it changes to focus on AI (computers that can think and write). SAP has not commented.
stories.why: It shows big companies are swapping some jobs for AI.
stories.sides: No major disagreement. Reuters says it could not confirm the report on its own yet.

quick_hits: Conservatives want Diana Fox Carney, the Prime Minister's wife, to tell Parliament about her ocean envoy job; Carney's office says it follows ethics rules.
PM Carney met Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe in Regina on Thursday.
A big US Thanksgiving storm brought floods and wind, and up to 13 inches of snow is expected near St. Louis.
big_picture: Israel's new government is still being stitched together, while AI keeps changing who gets hired.
